candidates.title: WAKMan: Workload Aware KVCache Manager
candidates.abstract: Prefix caching enables a Large Language Model (LLM) servers to reuse the Key-Value (KV) states and accelerate prefill computation stage for requests that share a prefix with earlier prompts, thus reducing latency and serving cost. With limited memory resource, the KV cache eviction policy becomes a decisive factor in determining the overall benefits of prefix caching. Production traffic may have single-turn, multi-turn, agentic, or a mixture of any combination of these request types. Our findings indicate that agentic steps return within seconds and favor recency, while popular prompts and long conversations return after many other requests and favor frequency. Across 20 mixes, no single policy is always best: vLLM's default strategy LRU provides 12% higher cache hits as compared to the frequency-oriented S3FIFO on agentic-heavy mixes but trails it by up to 22% elsewhere, and even a single workload parameter can flip the winner even for any particular mix. We present WAKMan, a workload-aware KV cache manager that picks its eviction policy from live traffic without knowing request types or reading prompts. It improves hit rate over LRU by 5 percentage points on average, with the lowest mean and worst-case optimality gap of all policies.
candidates.reason: ワークロード配慮型KVキャッシュ管理WAKMan。接頭辞キャッシュの排除方策が、単発・多ターン・エージェントなど混合した本番トラフィックで一律には最適にならないことを示し、ワークロードに応じて方策を使い分ける管理。推論メモリ機構そのもの。

candidates.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
candidates.abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.
candidates.reason: ツール配慮型の共同スケジューリングTAO。エージェント提供でツール戻りの準備状況を評価に含めず資源を無駄にする問題と、受理と配置のヒューリスティクスに対し、近い将来のツール準備・ノード別キャッシュクレジット・トークンフットプリントを合わせた価値界面と、動的計画法による共同の選択・配置を行う。推論基盤のスケジューリングそのもの。
